findings.passage: “I think we all recognize the fact that people here in Wisconsin enjoy the outdoors,” Pfaff said. “We’ve got a tremendous sporting heritage and it brings together families … as they enjoy the great deer hunt around Thanksgiving.”
findings.note: Radio interview with UpNorthNews during his 2022 congressional primary, quoted by that outlet. Asked about a ban on a type of firearm, he points to hunting heritage.

findings.passage: “I hear you on that,” he replied. “The thing is—the question becomes—when we begin to have a conversation, as far as we start talking about shotguns and rifles, we start talking about, you know, what is the definition? And that’s an important conversation to have. I mean, I have been very clear. There is no place for weapons of war on our streets.”
findings.note: Same interview, quoted by UpNorthNews. Asked whether hunting uses semi-automatic guns, he says the definition of the guns covered matters and that weapons of war have no place on streets. The outlet reports he gave indications he would oppose a ban; that is the outlet's reading, not his words.

findings.passage: ‘It is important, in our heritage and our culture. We recognize that. But we also recognize there’s common sense solutions that can be done. Like background checks. Like making sure that we do have red flag laws put in place. Making sure that we do fund mental health, which is so very important. These are things that are bipartisan—should be bipartisan. The vast majority of Wisconsin residents support this. This is common sense.’
findings.note: Quoted in a news roundup (the page quotes a local TV report) reposted on the state party's site, so the outlet is secondhand; event was in La Crosse on 2024-02-09 (page published 2024-02-12). He names background checks, red flag laws and mental health funding.

findings.passage: “This should not be a controversial topic, to insure that our children can go to school, go to a mall, or go to a movie theater without fear that it may be the last thing they do.”
findings.note: Quoted by WIZM at a La Crosse event on gun violence in schools; he calls for more gun safety laws.
